title: Cold rebuild: Compute a TOTP code
summary: Rebuild Compute a TOTP code from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Compute a TOTP code** in *MFA and stopping guessers*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Which 30-second window is each moment in? What does this print?
steps.explain: Integer division groups the seconds into windows of 30. Everyone whose clock reads within the same window computes the same code.

steps.title: Rebuild Compute a TOTP code cold
prompt: Write `string Totp(byte[] secret, long unixSeconds, int digits)` following RFC 6238 with HMAC-SHA1 and a 30-second step.
The RFC's own test vectors (secret is the ASCII text `12345678901234567890`, 8 digits):
With `digits = 6`, time 59 gives `287082`. Note the leading zero in `07081804`.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
string Totp(byte[] secret, long unixSeconds, int digits)
